clue.text: Spanish shop selling wine with a lot of body, mature, rounded

indicators.note: a lot of the word, but not all of it: the clue word body loses its final letter
rounded as in turned round, so the word for mature is written backwards

parts.note: to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A Spanish wine shop praises a full-bodied, well-aged, rounded red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter; 'rounded' turns the age word round. Body, mature and rounded read as wine-tasting terms, but each does mechanical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or small grocery that sells wine.

clue.text: French cheese contains new preservative fluid

indicators.note: the cheese holds the next piece within it, a container signal

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A French cheese is said to be packed with a liquid that keeps it fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt water, used for pickling and keeping food, is a preserving liquid.

clue.text: Carefully pours out sand etc and ends act drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so the letters of ends act are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy is pouring sand about carelessly at the close of a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals an anagram of ENDS ACT. The letters of 'sand etc' rearrange to the same answer too, a bonus inside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant is to pour gently from one container to another, leaving sediment behind.

clue.text: Drink spirit with a half of German beer

parts.note: gin is a spirit

indicators.note: only half the word German is used, its first three letters

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone orders a spirit alongside half a German beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger.

clue.text: Caught one on board making plain cakes

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the steamship letters surround the other pieces

parts.note: a ship is written SS (steamship) in crosswords, and being on board means inside it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has been caught bringing a snack aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means aboard a ship, written as the steamship abbreviation around the other pieces. Scones are small British teatime cakes, often served with jam and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones are simple unsweetened or lightly sweetened baked teatime cakes.

clue.text: Initially customers really enjoy summer salads with this ingredient

definitions.text: Initially customers really enjoy summer salads with this ingredient

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Diners are said to love summer salads containing a particular leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of customers, really, enjoy, summer, salads; the whole clue also describes the answer as a salad ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a peppery green leaf commonly added to salads and sandwiches.

clue.text: Beans go off in for example Arab's food container

indicators.note: off as in gone bad or out of order, telling us to rearrange the letters of beans go

explanation.surface: Some beans have gone bad inside an Arab's lunch box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of BEANS GO. The Arab here is a horse breed, not a person, which is why its food comes in a bag hung on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a feed bag strapped over a horse's muzzle, and an Arab is a breed of horse.

clue.text: Dessert based on biscuit dough needs not long to harden

parts.note: short is the opposite of long
to cake is to form a hard crust or set solid

explanation.surface: A cook explains that a biscuit-based pudding needs only a short time to set.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcake is a dessert of crumbly biscuit topped with fruit and cream.

clue.text: It's affected chopping up of meat

definitions.meaning: affected means pretentious or dainty in manner, as a walk or speech can be
the act of cutting meat into very small pieces in a grinder

explanation.surface: A butcher's prissy manner is likened to grinding beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty, over-refined walk is described with this word, which is also the act of finely chopping meat.

clue.text: Hopes at resort to find place for drinks and refreshment

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, to sort again, so the letters of hopes at are rearranged

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers at a seaside resort hope to find a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but means re-sort: rearrange HOPES AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea shop is a small café serving tea, cakes and light meals.

clue.text: Edible molluscs, slow movers in France, get across if cooked

definitions.text: Edible molluscs, slow movers in France

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered or prepared, so get across is rearranged

explanation.surface: A French recipe for snails, a slow-moving dish, if you can get across the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals the anagram of GET ACROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails eaten as food, especially in French cuisine with garlic butter, go by this French name.

clue.text: Corporate festive occasions have been pronounced slap-up meals

indicators.note: pronounced says the word is spoken, so we take its sound not its spelling

parts.note: the clue word been spoken aloud matches a vegetable's name
a slap-up meal is a lavish one, a feast

explanation.surface: Office parties are reported to have involved lavish dinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' turns BEEN into its sound-alike BEAN. A beanfeast (beano) is British slang for a works outing or celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast was traditionally an annual dinner an employer gave staff, now any jolly celebration.

clue.text: Eat into light meal (or live without it)

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter nibbles a snack, or manages without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. 'light meal' is a second definition of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bite into something is to cut into it with the teeth; a bite is also a snack.

clue.text: Finished with a dish popular in S. Europe

parts.note: something finished is over, in the past

explanation.surface: Someone has finished a plate of a southern European favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles such as spaghetti and penne, central to Italian cooking, make this dish.

clue.text: Prepare coffee for every company delayed

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
something delayed is late

explanation.surface: An office making coffee for every member of staff is running late.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew coffee by passing hot water repeatedly through the grounds is this process.

clue.text: The spirit in which each year Magna Carta is celebrated?

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: A question about the drink used each year to toast the charter of 1215.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'yeAR MAGNA Carta'. Magna Carta is the English charter of liberties sealed in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy from Gascony in south-west France, a distilled spirit.

clue.text: Cook in oven with very small flap

parts.note: micro means tiny, as in microscopic
to flap a hand is to wave it

explanation.surface: Someone cooks with a tiny oven door that flaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat food quickly in an appliance using electromagnetic radiation is this verb.

clue.text: Part of breakfast for example is in new fridge

indicators.note: is in tells us one piece sits inside the other
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of fridge

explanation.surface: An item for the morning meal is waiting in a new refrigerator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' scrambles the appliance's letters and 'is in' places the abbreviation inside them, splitting the scramble after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked in a pan of hot fat is a staple of the cooked breakfast.

clue.text: Concentrated essence is unusually beginning to clarify on time

parts.note: extra means unusually, as in extra careful

indicators.note: only the opening letter of clarify is used

explanation.surface: A distilled flavouring is said to start clearing up remarkably fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes C from clarify. 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal but supplies EXTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla or meat extract is a concentrated preparation drawn from a substance.

clue.text: Worry about first slice of venison that's cut

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the worry word goes around the next piece

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety

indicators.note: the first slice of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone frets over the first slice from a joint of deer meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first slice of' takes V from venison; 'about' puts CARE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To slice meat from a joint at the table is this verb.

clue.text: The fruits of fresh air peccadillos?

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new form, so the letters of air are rearranged

parts.note: peccadillos are minor sins

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what small outdoor misdeeds produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried grapes are fruits used in baking.

clue.text: Post-prandial drink left for naval officers

definitions.meaning: a fortified wine served after dinner
on a ship, the left-hand side is called by this name

explanation.surface: Ship's officers take an after-dinner drink, leaving it for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified Portuguese wine drunk after dinner; also the nautical term for a vessel's left side.

clue.text: Wash old organic meat? That takes the biscuit

parts.note: to bath is to wash
liver is an organ eaten as meat, offal

explanation.surface: A remark that washing elderly offal is the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That takes the biscuit' is an idiom for 'that beats everything', but literally names something that is a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bath Oliver is a plain dry English biscuit, so it literally takes the name of a biscuit.

clue.text: Brought home by successful folk although not one taxi to be raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: not one means no
a taxi is a cab

explanation.surface: Successful people walk home, not taking a single taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be raised' turns NO CAB upwards in the down entry. To 'bring home the bacon' is to earn a living.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'bring home the bacon' means earn money or succeed.

clue.text: Push what soldiers might have at breakfast

definitions.meaning: to urge or encourage someone on

definitions.text: what soldiers might have at breakfast
definitions.meaning: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a boiled egg

explanation.surface: Troops at breakfast are urged forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone is the phrasal verb; toast soldiers with yolk on them fits the second reading.

clue.text: Sauce label put on since by firm

parts.note: a tab is a small label or tag
as means since, as in as it was raining
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A sauce bottle's label has been put on by the manufacturer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot pepper condiment from Louisiana, sold under this brand name.

clue.text: Airline wants royalty on occasions when bread or cakes are cooked

definitions.text: occasions when bread or cakes are cooked

parts.note: BA stands for British Airways
kings are royalty

explanation.surface: An airline wants royal approval to cook its in-flight bread and cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Each batch put through the oven is one session of this kind.

clue.text: Warming system hasn't started off what diner is doing

indicators.note: the word lacks its opening letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a heating system warms a building

explanation.surface: The heating has failed to come on, a diner complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't started' removes the H from HEATING.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is someone having a meal, consuming food.

clue.text: Appropriate time to put salt and pepper on

definitions.meaning: a period of the year suited to something, as the hunting period

definitions.text: to put salt and pepper on

explanation.surface: A cook knows just when to add salt and pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of the year such as summer or the shooting period; also to flavour food with salt or spice.
